appraisal_events.evidence: vous devriez... apprendre... à vous abstenir d'exprimer des sentiments trop naturels... vous vous seriez évité d'avoir l'air de parler à tort et à travers comme un sourd et d'ajouter par là un second ridicule à celui d'avoir des ancres brodées sur votre costume de bain.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus delivers a cold, cutting rebuke that mocks the narrator's naive response and appearance, asserting clear rhetorical and social superiority over him.

appraisal_events.evidence: les histoires trop facilement trouvées drôles par notre camarade étaient des histoires de M. Bloch père, et que l'homme « tout à fait curieux » était toujours un de ses amis qu'il jugeait de cette façon.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's retrospective realization exposes Bloch's apparent wit and worldly judgments as derivative of his father's opinions, quietly deflating the precocious authority Bloch once held in the narrator's eyes.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is scolded and made to look foolish and ridiculous in Charlus's icy reproach.
Charlus explicitly faults the narrator's ability to respond thoughtfully, undercutting his standing in the exchange.
Bloch's admired wit and discernment are revealed as borrowed from his father, diminishing his prior appearance of originality.
Bloch's status as the more 'advanced' comrade whose judgments the narrator once deferred to is quietly undercut by this revelation of derivativeness.

ambiguities: Charlus's tirade is presented mostly through quoted speech; the following note that he 'sans doute eut... regret de ces paroles' hints the narrator may view the rebuke as excessive, so it is unclear whether the passage fully endorses Charlus's harshness as deserved or frames it with some critical distance.
